Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not use blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity and age of the offense. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and CRD regulations.

A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, plus first month's rent. Small landlords may take up to two months' rent unless the tenant is a service member. The remaining deposit and an itemized statement are due within 21 days after move-out. The current text was amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

No one may sell or use an algorithmic device to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. An algorithmic device is a tool, such as software, that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for a vacant unit. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and a landlord also needs just cause to remove certain housing services such as parking, storage or laundry. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

Tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's amount (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026) was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: S.F. Police Code Art. 49 (Fair Chance Ordinance).

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the rate set by the Rent Board, which is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier rates were 5.0% (2025–2026) and 5.2% (2024–2025). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Rent Board, Security Deposit Interest Rates (Rent Board topic 572).

A0073.explanation: Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Cambridge City Council policy order (number not stated).

Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected categories, including source of income such as Section 8 vouchers and public benefits. They may use reasonable selection standards, like ability to pay rent, only if applied equally to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. Senate Bill S.2983 (194th General Court).

Only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. At the first personal meeting, the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, the time and manner of payment, and whether the fee depends on a lease being signed. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended this to agents of the lessor and payments to them; the earlier text applied only to the lessor. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A broker fee for finding rental housing may be paid only by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally engaged and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A broker may contract either with a prospective tenant or with a landlord or landlord's agent, and only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge a fee for finding dwelling accommodations for tenants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements and give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions. Courts may not accept a nonpayment eviction filing without proof that the form was delivered. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 31.

When a tenant under a written lease fails to pay rent due, the landlord must give a written 14-day notice to quit to end the lease. The lease is not ended if the tenant pays or tenders all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in the landlord's possession action. This section sets notice and cure rules for nonpayment; it does not create a general just-cause requirement. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice equal to the longer of the rent payment interval or 30 days (three months if rent is paid less often). For nonpayment, a landlord may give a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone providing rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not take a security deposit larger than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (minus allowed, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0074.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The fee may be charged only if the landlord uses a first-come screening process or refunds fees to applicants not selected; the landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report. This text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9, not the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing owners may not discriminate against or harass any person because of source of income (including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers) or other protected traits, or publish ads showing such a preference. Where there is a government rent subsidy, owners must base income standards on the tenant's share of the rent and may not use credit history without offering the applicant the option of giving alternative evidence of ability to pay. The current text was amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776 (SB 267), effective January 1, 2024. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity and age of the offense. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and CRD regulations.

The remaining deposit and an itemized statement are due within 21 days after move-out. The current text was amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Los Angeles Council File 24-1031 (Motion, Hutt).

Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed at-fault reasons (e.g., nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal of access) or no-fault reasons (owner/family move-in, resident manager, demolition/removal from market, government order, conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require relocation assistance, and all termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.09.

Landlords of covered rental units in Los Angeles may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause. Landlords must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction within 5 years of filing a Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict must meet the RPO relocation requirements. Lower-income tenants receive enhanced payments, and all tenants receive at least the RSO or JCO amounts. Other protections include a right to remain up to 6 months before construction, a right to return, and a right of first refusal. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance).

For units under the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, the annual allowable rent increase for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 is 3%. Beginning February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add any extra percentage increase for utilities. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

The RSO requires interest payments on security deposits for RSO rental units; this page lists the requirement but does not state the rate or timing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance).

A0078.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban can be enforced by the city and by private parties, with fines up to $2,000 per day. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rents in covered rental properties under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt. This page does not state the allowed increase amount; it links to a Consumer Price Index chart. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Municipal Code Chapter 260.
Enacted, but takes effect 2027-07-01, after 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 56:9-20 to 56:9-26 (P.L. 2026, c.43, §4).

A landlord or landlord's agent may not require an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the statutory good causes, and must serve the required notices to cease and notices to quit. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap. A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must follow any local rent control ordinance. A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease and must end the old lease with written notice and offer a new lease at the higher rent. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f).
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental housing based on protected characteristics, including source of lawful income. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g)-(h).

Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until they make a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment shows withdrawal is necessary for a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. Arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records and juvenile adjudications may never be considered, and drug or alcohol testing of applicants is banned. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

Landlords must hold deposits in trust in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey institution (or permitted money market fund for larger landlords), pay the interest to the tenant annually, and give written notice of where the deposit is held. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-19.

Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear and money owed under the lease; within 5 business days if the tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1.

A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent; prepaid rent, last month's rent and pet deposits count toward the cap, and yearly deposit increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

The act applies to all rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes. Owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units are exempt unless the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity and age of the offense. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and CRD regulations.

A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, plus first month's rent. Small landlords may take up to two months' rent unless the tenant is a service member. The remaining deposit and an itemized statement are due within 21 days after move-out. The current text was amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Los Angeles Council File 24-1031 (Motion, Hutt).

Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed at-fault reasons (e.g., nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal of access) or no-fault reasons (owner/family move-in, resident manager, demolition/removal from market, government order, conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require relocation assistance, and all termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.09.

Landlords of covered rental units in Los Angeles may end a tenancy only for a listed at-fault or no-fault just cause. Landlords must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction within 5 years of filing a Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict must meet the RPO relocation requirements. Lower-income tenants receive enhanced payments, and all tenants receive at least the RSO or JCO amounts. Other protections include a right to remain up to 6 months before construction, a right to return, and a right of first refusal. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance).

For units under the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, the annual allowable rent increase for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 is 3%. Beginning February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add any extra percentage increase for utilities. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

The RSO requires interest payments on security deposits for RSO rental units; this page lists the requirement but does not state the rate or timing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance).

A0080.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The fee may be charged only if the landlord uses a first-come screening process or refunds fees to applicants not selected; the landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report. This text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9, not the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

No one may sell or use an algorithmic device to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. An algorithmic device is a tool, such as software, that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for a vacant unit. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and a landlord also needs just cause to remove certain housing services such as parking, storage or laundry. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

Tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's amount (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026) was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: S.F. Police Code Art. 49 (Fair Chance Ordinance).

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the rate set by the Rent Board, which is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier rates were 5.0% (2025–2026) and 5.2% (2024–2025). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Rent Board, Security Deposit Interest Rates (Rent Board topic 572).

A0082.explanation: Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Cambridge City Council policy order (number not stated).

Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected categories, including source of income such as Section 8 vouchers and public benefits. They may use reasonable selection standards, like ability to pay rent, only if applied equally to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. Senate Bill S.2983 (194th General Court).

Only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. At the first personal meeting, the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, the time and manner of payment, and whether the fee depends on a lease being signed. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended this to agents of the lessor and payments to them; the earlier text applied only to the lessor. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A broker fee for finding rental housing may be paid only by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally engaged and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A broker may contract either with a prospective tenant or with a landlord or landlord's agent, and only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge a fee for finding dwelling accommodations for tenants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements and give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions. Courts may not accept a nonpayment eviction filing without proof that the form was delivered. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 31.

When a tenant under a written lease fails to pay rent due, the landlord must give a written 14-day notice to quit to end the lease. The lease is not ended if the tenant pays or tenders all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in the landlord's possession action. This section sets notice and cure rules for nonpayment; it does not create a general just-cause requirement. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice equal to the longer of the rent payment interval or 30 days (three months if rent is paid less often). For nonpayment, a landlord may give a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone providing rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not take a security deposit larger than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (minus allowed, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0083.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.

Covered housing providers may not use a blanket ban on applicants with arrests or convictions and must judge applicants case by case. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when deciding eligibility or eviction, and may not use credit scores to approve or deny applicants. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017).

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate against renters because they use rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is an example of illegal housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.

The current text was amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776 (SB 267), effective January 1, 2024. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not use blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity and age of the offense. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and CRD regulations.

A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, plus first month's rent. Small landlords may take up to two months' rent unless the tenant is a service member. The remaining deposit and an itemized statement are due within 21 days after move-out. The current text was amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

No one may sell or use an algorithmic device to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. An algorithmic device is a tool, such as software, that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for a vacant unit. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and a landlord also needs just cause to remove certain housing services such as parking, storage or laundry. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

Tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's amount (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026) was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: S.F. Police Code Art. 49 (Fair Chance Ordinance).

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the rate set by the Rent Board, which is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier rates were 5.0% (2025–2026) and 5.2% (2024–2025). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Rent Board, Security Deposit Interest Rates (Rent Board topic 572).

A0086.explanation: Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Cambridge City Council policy order (number not stated).

Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected categories, including source of income such as Section 8 vouchers and public benefits. They may use reasonable selection standards, like ability to pay rent, only if applied equally to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. Senate Bill S.2983 (194th General Court).

Only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. At the first personal meeting, the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, the time and manner of payment, and whether the fee depends on a lease being signed. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended this to agents of the lessor and payments to them; the earlier text applied only to the lessor. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A broker fee for finding rental housing may be paid only by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally engaged and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A broker may contract either with a prospective tenant or with a landlord or landlord's agent, and only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge a fee for finding dwelling accommodations for tenants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements and give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions. Courts may not accept a nonpayment eviction filing without proof that the form was delivered. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 31.

When a tenant under a written lease fails to pay rent due, the landlord must give a written 14-day notice to quit to end the lease. The lease is not ended if the tenant pays or tenders all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in the landlord's possession action. This section sets notice and cure rules for nonpayment; it does not create a general just-cause requirement. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice equal to the longer of the rent payment interval or 30 days (three months if rent is paid less often). For nonpayment, a landlord may give a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone providing rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not take a security deposit larger than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (minus allowed, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0087.explanation: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Nonpublic competitor information is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-2.

Rents in covered dwellings are controlled at the base rent received as of October 1, 1985, and no increase may be demanded or accepted except as the chapter allows; excess increases are void and must be refunded or credited. Landlords must give tenants a Board-approved disclosure statement of their rights, and tenants must request a legal rent calculation within two years of service of that statement to get a refund. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 155-4.

When a lease expires or a periodic tenancy ends, a landlord may not request or receive a rent increase greater than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less. Only one such cost-of-living increase is allowed in any 12-month period, regardless of how many tenants occupy the unit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 155-5.

Residential landlords who raise rent by more than 10% year over year when renewing a current tenant's lease must give the tenant written disclosures before the increase takes effect. The disclosures go either on the first page of the renewal lease or on a Hoboken Division of Housing form. They must include an itemization of costs, whether a rent algorithm was used, the tenant's right to take legal action, and Division of Housing contact information. This rule does not cap the increase itself. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-1.

When a tenant leaves voluntarily or is legally evicted, a registered unit may be decontrolled for the new tenant's first rental. That first rent may not be more than 25% above the last rent paid, not counting capital improvement surcharges. Later increases are again controlled, and a unit may be decontrolled no more than once every three years. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code §§ 155-31 to 155-34.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Hoboken City Code Ch. 155, §§ 155-2, 155-25.
Enacted, but takes effect 2027-07-01, after 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 56:9-20 to 56:9-26 (P.L. 2026, c.43, §4).

A landlord or landlord's agent may not require an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the statutory good causes, and must serve the required notices to cease and notices to quit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap. A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must follow any local rent control ordinance. A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease and must end the old lease with written notice and offer a new lease at the higher rent. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f).
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental housing based on protected characteristics, including source of lawful income. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g)-(h).

Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until they make a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment shows withdrawal is necessary for a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. Arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records and juvenile adjudications may never be considered, and drug or alcohol testing of applicants is banned. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

Landlords must hold deposits in trust in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey institution (or permitted money market fund for larger landlords), pay the interest to the tenant annually, and give written notice of where the deposit is held. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-19.

Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear and money owed under the lease; within 5 business days if the tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1.

A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent; prepaid rent, last month's rent and pet deposits count toward the cap, and yearly deposit increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

The act applies to all rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes. Owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units are exempt unless the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0088.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The fee may be charged only if the landlord uses a first-come screening process or refunds fees to applicants not selected; the landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report. This text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

This amending ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025; the document does not state the final adoption or effective date. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code Ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S..

Berkeley owners who charge an applicant a fee for a credit report or to process an application must first give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement. They must also state the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The disclosure goes either in the application or in a separate disclosure before the fee is received. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010.

Owners and agents may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016.

Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, and qualifying households get an additional $6,471. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance.

Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for nonpayment unless the tenant owes at least one month's HUD Fair Market Rent, and bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease. It also tightens lease-breach evictions and requires notice contents and filing of notices with the Rent Board within three business days. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The fee may be charged only if the landlord uses a first-come screening process or refunds fees to applicants not selected; the landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report. This text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9, not the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing owners may not discriminate against or harass any person because of source of income (including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers) or other protected traits, or publish ads showing such a preference. Where there is a government rent subsidy, owners must base income standards on the tenant's share of the rent and may not use credit history without offering the applicant the option of giving alternative evidence of ability to pay. The current text was amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776 (SB 267), effective January 1, 2024. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not use blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity and age of the offense. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and CRD regulations.

A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, plus first month's rent. Small landlords may take up to two months' rent unless the tenant is a service member. The remaining deposit and an itemized statement are due within 21 days after move-out. The current text was amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

No one may sell or use an algorithmic device to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. An algorithmic device is a tool, such as software, that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for a vacant unit. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and a landlord also needs just cause to remove certain housing services such as parking, storage or laundry. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

Tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's amount (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026) was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: S.F. Police Code Art. 49 (Fair Chance Ordinance).

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the rate set by the Rent Board, which is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier rates were 5.0% (2025–2026) and 5.2% (2024–2025). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Rent Board, Security Deposit Interest Rates (Rent Board topic 572).

A0098.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.

Covered housing providers may not use a blanket ban on applicants with arrests or convictions and must judge applicants case by case. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when deciding eligibility or eviction, and may not use credit scores to approve or deny applicants. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017).

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate against renters because they use rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is an example of illegal housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. Senate Bill S.2983 (194th General Court).

Only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. At the first personal meeting, the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, the time and manner of payment, and whether the fee depends on a lease being signed. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended this to agents of the lessor and payments to them; the earlier text applied only to the lessor. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A broker fee for finding rental housing may be paid only by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally engaged and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A broker may contract either with a prospective tenant or with a landlord or landlord's agent, and only licensed brokers or salespeople may charge a fee for finding dwelling accommodations for tenants. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements and give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions. Courts may not accept a nonpayment eviction filing without proof that the form was delivered. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 31.

When a tenant under a written lease fails to pay rent due, the landlord must give a written 14-day notice to quit to end the lease. The lease is not ended if the tenant pays or tenders all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in the landlord's possession action. This section sets notice and cure rules for nonpayment; it does not create a general just-cause requirement. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 11.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice equal to the longer of the rent payment interval or 30 days (three months if rent is paid less often). For nonpayment, a landlord may give a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone providing rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not take a security deposit larger than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (minus allowed, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0099.explanation: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Nonpublic competitor information is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-2.

Rents in covered dwellings are controlled at the base rent received as of October 1, 1985, and no increase may be demanded or accepted except as the chapter allows; excess increases are void and must be refunded or credited. Landlords must give tenants a Board-approved disclosure statement of their rights, and tenants must request a legal rent calculation within two years of service of that statement to get a refund. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 155-4.

When a lease expires or a periodic tenancy ends, a landlord may not request or receive a rent increase greater than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less. Only one such cost-of-living increase is allowed in any 12-month period, regardless of how many tenants occupy the unit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 155-5.

Residential landlords who raise rent by more than 10% year over year when renewing a current tenant's lease must give the tenant written disclosures before the increase takes effect. The disclosures go either on the first page of the renewal lease or on a Hoboken Division of Housing form. They must include an itemization of costs, whether a rent algorithm was used, the tenant's right to take legal action, and Division of Housing contact information. This rule does not cap the increase itself. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-1.

When a tenant leaves voluntarily or is legally evicted, a registered unit may be decontrolled for the new tenant's first rental. That first rent may not be more than 25% above the last rent paid, not counting capital improvement surcharges. Later increases are again controlled, and a unit may be decontrolled no more than once every three years. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code §§ 155-31 to 155-34.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Hoboken City Code Ch. 155, §§ 155-2, 155-25.
Enacted, but takes effect 2027-07-01, after 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 56:9-20 to 56:9-26 (P.L. 2026, c.43, §4).

A landlord or landlord's agent may not require an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the statutory good causes, and must serve the required notices to cease and notices to quit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap. A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must follow any local rent control ordinance. A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease and must end the old lease with written notice and offer a new lease at the higher rent. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f).
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental housing based on protected characteristics, including source of lawful income. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g)-(h).

Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until they make a conditional offer. After the offer they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment shows withdrawal is necessary for a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. Arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records and juvenile adjudications may never be considered, and drug or alcohol testing of applicants is banned. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

Landlords must hold deposits in trust in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey institution (or permitted money market fund for larger landlords), pay the interest to the tenant annually, and give written notice of where the deposit is held. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-19.

Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear and money owed under the lease; within 5 business days if the tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1.

A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent; prepaid rent, last month's rent and pet deposits count toward the cap, and yearly deposit increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

The act applies to all rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes. Owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units are exempt unless the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

Proposed ordinance that would make it unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. It would also bar anyone from selling, licensing or providing such a device to a landlord. An algorithmic device is software that uses nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rents or occupancy levels. Per the ordinance text, it would take effect 30 days after final passage; this document leaves the passage date blank. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.1101–98.1104 (proposed Ordinance O-2025-107).
Coverage depends on year built, government subsidized, owner occupied, owner is corporation, which the public records do not include. Source: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.0701–98.0710.

A0101.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban can be enforced by the city and by private parties, with fines up to $2,000 per day. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rents in covered rental properties under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt. This page does not state the allowed increase amount; it links to a Consumer Price Index chart. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Municipal Code Chapter 260.

A0103.explanation: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (software that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old to recommend rents, fees, occupancy or other lease terms) when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units, and no one may sell, license or provide such an algorithm to Berkeley landlords. This amending ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025; the document does not state the final adoption or effective date. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code Ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S..

Berkeley owners who charge an applicant a fee for a credit report or to process an application must first give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement. They must also state the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The disclosure goes either in the application or in a separate disclosure before the fee is received. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010.

Owners and agents may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016.

Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, and qualifying households get an additional $6,471. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance.

Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for nonpayment unless the tenant owes at least one month's HUD Fair Market Rent, and bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease. It also tightens lease-breach evictions and requires notice contents and filing of notices with the Rent Board within three business days. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024).

Owners who evict a tenant for an owner move-in must pay the tenant relocation assistance. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, and qualifying households get an additional $6,471. Amounts are adjusted each year for inflation. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance.

Eligible landlords may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by no more than 1.0% under the 2026 Annual General Adjustment, starting no earlier than January 1, 2026. Source: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A.

Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about, require disclosure of, or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions. A landlord who takes any action based on criminal history must give written notice and a chance to respond. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.106.

The act applies to all rental premises or units used for dwelling purposes. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0109.explanation: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (software that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old to recommend rents, fees, occupancy or other lease terms) when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units, and no one may sell, license or provide such an algorithm to Berkeley landlords. This amending ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025; the document does not state the final adoption or effective date. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code Ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S..

Berkeley owners who charge an applicant a fee for a credit report or to process an application must first give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement. They must also state the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The disclosure goes either in the application or in a separate disclosure before the fee is received. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010.

Owners and agents may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016.

Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, and qualifying households get an additional $6,471. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance.

Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for nonpayment unless the tenant owes at least one month's HUD Fair Market Rent, and bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease. It also tightens lease-breach evictions and requires notice contents and filing of notices with the Rent Board within three business days. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024).

Owners who evict a tenant for an owner move-in must pay the tenant relocation assistance. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, and qualifying households get an additional $6,471. Amounts are adjusted each year for inflation. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024).
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance.

Eligible landlords may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by no more than 1.0% under the 2026 Annual General Adjustment, starting no earlier than January 1, 2026. The AGA equals 65% of the Bay Area CPI increase for July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025, which was 1.5%. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A.

Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about, require disclosure of, or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, ending a tenancy, charging a higher deposit or rent, or refusing to add an immediate family member because of criminal history. A landlord who takes any action based on criminal history must give written notice and a chance to respond. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.106.

For units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year, and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The fee may be charged only if the landlord uses a first-come screening process or refunds fees to applicants not selected; the landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report. This text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, year built, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9, not the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, year built, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing owners may not discriminate against or harass any person because of source of income (including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers) or other protected traits, or publish ads showing such a preference. Where there is a government rent subsidy, owners must base income standards on the tenant's share of the rent and may not use credit history without offering the applicant the option of giving alternative evidence of ability to pay. The current text was amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 776 (SB 267), effective January 1, 2024. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not use blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity and age of the offense. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and CRD regulations.

A landlord may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent, plus first month's rent. Small landlords may take up to two months' rent unless the tenant is a service member. The remaining deposit and an itemized statement are due within 21 days after move-out. The current text was amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and a landlord also needs just cause to remove certain housing services such as parking, storage or laundry. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

Tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must receive relocation payments. For eviction notices served March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027, the amount is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent.
